proposedTopics.title: Errors & reverts
proposedTopics.description: How Solidity signals failure and rolls back: require/revert/assert, custom errors, and the Error(string) / Panic(uint) selectors the EVM returns.

proposedTopics.title: ETH transfer
proposedTopics.description: Receiving and sending native ETH: payable, msg.value, transfer/send/call, and the receive/fallback special functions. The most reentrancy-prone corner of the language.

proposedTopics.title: Low-level calls
proposedTopics.description: The raw call/delegatecall/staticcall primitives and try/catch — how contracts talk to other contracts, the storage-context trap of delegatecall, and the read-only guarantee of staticcall.

proposedTopics.title: ABI encoding & decoding
proposedTopics.description: How arguments are serialized for calls and hashes: abi.encode vs encodePacked, abi.decode, function selectors, and encodeCall/encodeWithSelector. Collision-safety matters.

proposedTopics.title: Hashing
proposedTopics.description: keccak256 as Ethereum's universal hash — mappings, merkle proofs, selectors, and commit-reveal — and the encode-vs-encodePacked collision trap when hashing.

proposedTopics.title: Signatures (ECDSA & EIP-712)
proposedTopics.description: Verifying off-chain authorizations on-chain: ecrecover, malleability, the EIP-191 prefix, and EIP-712 typed structured data with a domain separator for safe, human-readable signing.

proposedTopics.title: Libraries & interfaces
proposedTopics.description: Reusable libraries (using-for; internal functions compiled into the caller, public/external functions delegatecalled) and interfaces for type-safe cross-contract calls.

proposedTopics.title: Assembly & Yul intro
proposedTopics.description: Dropping to inline assembly (Yul): raw opcodes, the memory model (free pointer, scratch space), and direct storage access — power at the cost of every safety check.

proposedTopics.title: Transient storage
proposedTopics.description: EIP-1153's TSTORE/TLOAD: cheap storage that lives for one transaction then auto-clears — ideal for reentrancy locks and transient accumulators.

proposedTopics.title: User-defined value types
proposedTopics.description: UDVTs wrap an elementary type in a new, distinct compile-time type (Duration is uint256) for zero-cost type safety without arithmetic operators unless you add them.

proposedTopics.title: Custom errors
proposedTopics.description: Custom errors (error InsufficientBalance(uint have, uint want); revert InsufficientBalance(...)) replace revert strings since 0.8.4: the revert data is a 4-byte selector plus ABI-encoded arguments, far cheaper to deploy and revert with than a string. They also give callers structured, decodable failure data, and modern Solidity supports require(cond, CustomError()).
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Errors.sol with a withdraw guarded by a custom error carrying (have, want), with a test in test/phase02/Errors.t.sol using vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(...)). Done when: forge test passes and the test decodes the error's arguments from the revert data.

requirements.purpose: Learn the current declaration, revert/require usage, ABI shape, and gas rationale for custom errors.

options.title: Solidity documentation — Custom Errors
options.why: The maintained language reference shows both revert and require forms, named arguments, selector access, and how error data is ABI-encoded, directly covering the implementation and decoding test.

proposedTopics.title: require, revert & assert
proposedTopics.description: require validates inputs and preconditions and can revert with empty data, Error(string), or a custom error; revert provides unconditional early exit with the same error choices. assert checks invariants that should never fail and returns Panic(uint) — e.g. 0x11 overflow, 0x12 divide-by-zero, 0x32 array out-of-bounds. Since 0.8 a failed assert reverts without consuming all remaining gas. A triggered assert means a bug, never a user error.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Guards.sol with a require input check, a revert branch, and an assert invariant, with a test in test/phase02/Guards.t.sol asserting each failure's selector. Done when: forge test passes and the test distinguishes an Error(string) revert from a Panic(0x11) on overflow.

requirements.purpose: Distinguish recoverable input failures from invariant panics and recognize their exact revert-data forms.

proposedTopics.title: payable functions & msg.value
proposedTopics.description: A function must be marked payable to accept ETH; a non-payable function reverts if sent value. msg.value (in wei) is the amount attached to the current call and is visible to internal calls in the same execution context, while address(this).balance is the contract's total. Forgetting payable, or double-counting msg.value across internal calls, are common mistakes.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Payable.sol with a payable deposit that credits a balance mapping and a getBalance view of address(this).balance, with a test in test/phase02/Payable.t.sol. Done when: forge test passes and the test proves sending value to a non-payable function reverts and deposit credits msg.value.

requirements.purpose: Identify msg.value's unit and how message context changes across external versus internal calls.

proposedTopics.title: Sending ETH: transfer, send, call
proposedTopics.description: Three ways to send ETH differ in gas and error handling: transfer forwards a fixed 2300-gas stipend and reverts on failure; send does the same but returns a bool you must check; call{value: x}("") forwards the available gas by default and returns (bool, bytes). Current Solidity documentation deprecates transfer and send because fixed-stipend assumptions break as opcode costs change; use call with explicit failure handling, checks-effects-interactions, or a reentrancy guard.

Done when: forge test passes and the test asserts a failed call reverts through explicit failure handling rather than silently continuing.

requirements.purpose: Compare transfer, send, and call by gas forwarding, return value, failure behavior, and current deprecation status.

proposedTopics.title: receive & fallback
proposedTopics.description: receive() external payable runs when the contract is sent plain ETH with empty calldata; fallback() external [payable] runs when no function selector matches (or when ETH arrives with data and there is no receive). The dispatch rule: empty calldata + a receive present → receive, otherwise → fallback. A contract with neither cannot accept plain transfers, though protocol balance credits or selfdestruct can force ETH without a message call.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Fallback.sol with both receive and fallback logging which one ran, with a test in test/phase02/Fallback.t.sol sending empty vs non-matching calldata. Done when: forge test passes and the test proves empty calldata hits receive and unknown-selector calldata hits fallback.

requirements.purpose: Apply Solidity's exact empty-calldata, unknown-selector, and payable dispatch rules.

proposedTopics.title: Low-level call
proposedTopics.description: addr.call{value, gas}(abi.encodeWithSelector(...)) is the type-unsafe primitive that forwards a raw payload and returns (bool success, bytes returndata) WITHOUT reverting on failure — you must check success yourself. It also does not verify the target has code: calling an EOA or empty address returns success = true with empty data. This is the escape hatch when you don't have the callee's ABI, at the cost of every compiler guarantee.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/LowCall.sol invoking a target function via call and reverting on !success, with a test in test/phase02/LowCall.t.sol. Done when: forge test passes and the test proves an unchecked call to a reverting target would silently continue unless success is checked.

requirements.purpose: Learn raw call payload construction, gas/value options, and the success/returndata result tuple.

proposedTopics.title: delegatecall & storage context
proposedTopics.description: delegatecall runs the target's code in the CALLER's context: the caller's storage is read and written, and msg.sender/msg.value are preserved from the original call. This is the mechanism behind every proxy, but it demands that the proxy's and implementation's storage layouts match slot-for-slot — a mismatch makes the implementation write to the wrong slots and corrupt state. address(this) is the caller, not the code's contract.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Delegate.sol as a proxy-like caller and a logic contract that sets a uint and address, with a test in test/phase02/Delegate.t.sol proving the caller's storage changes. Done when: forge test passes and the test asserts the logic wrote into the caller's slots and msg.sender inside the logic equals the original caller.

requirements.purpose: Understand which code, address, balance, storage, msg.sender, and msg.value delegatecall uses.

options.title: Solidity documentation — Delegatecall and Libraries

proposedTopics.title: staticcall & read-only enforcement
proposedTopics.description: staticcall is like call but the EVM reverts the sub-call if it attempts any state change — SSTORE, log emission, contract creation, selfdestruct, or a value-bearing call. It is how external view functions are invoked, guaranteeing a call cannot mutate state behind your back. If you invoke a 'view' function through a raw call instead of staticcall, that guarantee is gone.

Done when: forge test passes and the test proves the read succeeds and the state-writing staticcall reverts.

requirements.purpose: Connect Solidity external view calls to EVM-level STATICCALL enforcement and its limits.

proposedTopics.title: try/catch for external calls
proposedTopics.description: try/catch handles reverts from an external call or a new-contract creation only — not internal/private calls. You can branch on catch Error(string reason) (a revert/require string), catch Panic(uint code) (an assert/arithmetic panic), catch (bytes lowLevelData) (custom errors and everything else), or a bare catch. It lets a caller recover instead of bubbling the callee's failure.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/TryCatch.sol calling an external contract that can revert with a string, a panic, or a custom error, with a test in test/phase02/TryCatch.t.sol hitting each catch arm. Done when: forge test passes and the test asserts the Error(string) reason and the Panic code are captured separately.

proposedTopics.title: abi.encode vs encodePacked
proposedTopics.description: abi.encode uses standard ABI head/tail encoding with 32-byte words, producing canonical bytes that can be decoded with a known schema; abi.encodePacked concatenates a compact representation without dynamic lengths, which is ambiguous for adjacent dynamic types. Because encodePacked(("a"),("bc")) equals encodePacked(("ab"),("c")), hashing packed user-controlled dynamic arguments can collide — a real authorization-bypass vector. Use encode when the bytes feed a security-relevant hash.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/AbiEncode.sol with both encoders and a function hashing two strings each way, with a test in test/phase02/AbiEncode.t.sol demonstrating the packed collision. Done when: forge test passes and the test proves two different string pairs produce the SAME encodePacked hash but DIFFERENT encode hashes.

requirements.purpose: Compare standard ABI encoding with packed layout and reproduce ambiguity between adjacent dynamic values.

proposedTopics.title: abi.decode & function selectors
proposedTopics.description: abi.decode(data, (uint, address)) reverses abi.encode back into typed values. A function selector is the first 4 bytes of keccak256 of the canonical signature ("transfer(address,uint256)"); calldata is selector ++ abi.encode(args). Prefer abi.encodeCall(IERC20.transfer, (to, amt)) — it is type-checked at compile time — over abi.encodeWithSignature, whose string signature typos slip through silently.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/AbiDecode.sol that encodes a struct+array with abi.encode, decodes it back, and builds a call payload with abi.encodeCall, with a test in test/phase02/AbiDecode.t.sol. Done when: forge test passes and the test asserts the round-trip decode equals the input and the selector equals bytes4(keccak256(sig)).

requirements.purpose: Derive the four-byte selector from a canonical signature and place standard-encoded arguments after it.

proposedTopics.title: keccak256 hashing
proposedTopics.description: keccak256(bytes) is Ethereum's workhorse 256-bit hash (the pre-standard Keccak, not NIST SHA3-256) — deterministic, one-way, collision-resistant — and underlies mapping slots, merkle proofs, function selectors, commit-reveal, and signatures. You hash by first ABI-encoding the inputs, and the choice of encode vs encodePacked changes the digest and the collision risk.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Keccak.sol with a commit-reveal (commit = keccak256(abi.encode(secret, salt))) plus a reveal check, with a test in test/phase02/Keccak.t.sol. proposedTopics.title: ECDSA signatures & ecrecover
proposedTopics.description: ecrecover(hash, v, r, s) returns the address that signed hash, or address(0) on failure — so you MUST reject a zero return, otherwise a bad signature 'authorizes' address(0). Signatures are malleable: for any valid (r, s) there is a second valid (r, n−s), so enforce low-s and add a nonce/deadline to stop replay. Off-chain signers hash the EIP-191 prefixed message ("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32"); use OpenZeppelin's ECDSA and MessageHashUtils libraries to get these checks right.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/VerifySig.sol recovering a signer with the EIP-191 prefix and rejecting address(0), with a test in test/phase02/VerifySig.t.sol using vm.sign. Done when: forge test passes and the test proves a valid signature recovers the expected signer and a tampered message does not.

requirements.purpose: Verify ecrecover's parameters, zero-address failure result, and unchanged high-s malleability behavior.

proposedTopics.title: EIP-712 typed structured data
proposedTopics.description: EIP-712 makes signed structured data inspectable and domain-separated by hashing a typed struct with a domain such as name, version, chainId, and verifyingContract. The digest is keccak256("\x19\x01" ++ domainSeparator ++ hashStruct(message)). Domain fields prevent cross-chain or cross-contract reuse when included, but EIP-712 does not itself stop replay of the same message within one domain; applications still need a nonce, deadline, or idempotent action.

Done when: forge test passes and the test proves a signature valid for this contract's domain fails verification when the chainId in the domain is changed.

requirements.purpose: Derive hashStruct, the domain separator, and the 0x1901 digest while separating domain reuse from same-domain replay.

proposedTopics.title: Libraries & using-for
proposedTopics.description: A library is reusable code without its own declared state; it cannot receive ETH normally or be destroyed. internal library functions are compiled into the caller's bytecode, while public/external ones use a deployed library through DELEGATECALL, running in the caller's context. using Lib for Type attaches compatible library functions as methods on that type.

requirements.purpose: Distinguish internal versus deployed library calls and attach compatible functions with using-for.

proposedTopics.title: Interfaces
proposedTopics.description: An interface declares external function signatures and can include ABI-visible types, events, and errors, but no function bodies, state variables, constructor, or modifiers; its functions are implicitly virtual. You wrap an address as IToken(addr) for type-checked high-level calls, and type(IToken).interfaceId gives the ERC-165 selector XOR. The interface is a compile-time promise, not runtime proof that the target conforms.

Done when: forge test passes and the test drives the Counter entirely through the interface type.

proposedTopics.title: Calling other contracts
proposedTopics.description: The high-level way to call another contract is Contract(addr).f(args) or Interface(addr).f(args): the compiler ABI-encodes the arguments, performs a CALL, checks the callee has code (or relies on return-data decoding), and bubbles up failures automatically. This is safer than raw call but still trusts the target's declared ABI — a wrong interface encodes and interprets data according to the wrong schema.

proposedTopics.title: Inline assembly & Yul basics
proposedTopics.description: An assembly { } block drops into Yul, giving direct access to memory, storage, calldata, and wrapping arithmetic without Solidity's usual type and overflow checks. It is used for low-level operations or measured optimizations. You must respect scratch space 0x00–0x3f, the free-memory pointer stored at 0x40–0x5f, and the zero slot at 0x60–0x7f or risk corrupting surrounding Solidity allocations.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Asm.sol with an assembly add and a mload/mstore round-trip that reads and restores the free memory pointer, with a test in test/phase02/Asm.t.sol. Done when: forge test passes and the test asserts the assembly result equals the Solidity equivalent.

requirements.purpose: Enter Yul from Solidity, use its basic operations, and recognize which compiler safety checks assembly bypasses.

proposedTopics.title: Storage & memory access in assembly
proposedTopics.description: In Yul, sload(slot)/sstore(slot,val) read and write storage directly, while mload/mstore/mstore8 operate on memory and keccak256(ptr, len) hashes a memory region. For a value-type mapping key, the entry slot is keccak256 over the 32-byte-padded key followed by the 32-byte base slot, equivalent to keccak256(abi.encode(key, baseSlot)). A wrong slot or damaged memory pointer can silently corrupt unrelated state or allocations.

Done when: forge test passes and the test asserts the assembly-read value equals the Solidity getter and the computed mapping slot holds the stored value.

proposedTopics.title: Transient storage (EIP-1153)
proposedTopics.description: EIP-1153 adds TSTORE/TLOAD — contract-private state that persists for one transaction and is discarded at its end. Each opcode currently costs 100 gas, avoiding persistent storage's disk access and refund accounting. Values survive across nested frames owned by the same contract, making transient storage useful for reentrancy locks and transaction-scoped accumulators. Solidity supports value-type transient state variables from 0.8.28 and tstore/tload in assembly; a composable lock must still reset before returning because clearing happens at end-of-transaction, not end-of-call.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Transient.sol with a reentrancy guard backed by transient storage, with a test in test/phase02/Transient.t.sol that reenters. Done when: forge test passes and the test proves a reentrant call reverts and a second independent transaction succeeds (the lock cleared).

requirements.purpose: Verify TLOAD/TSTORE lifetime, ownership, revert behavior, gas cost, and static-call restriction at protocol level.

proposedTopics.title: Defining a UDVT with wrap/unwrap
proposedTopics.description: type Duration is uint256 defines a user-defined value type — a new, distinct type over an elementary one, converted only via Duration.wrap(x) and Duration.unwrap(d). It costs nothing at runtime (the ABI uses the underlying value) but stops you from accidentally mixing, say, a Price and a Quantity that are both uint256. A UDVT has no operators or implicit conversions by default; operators can be defined through a global using-for directive, but this adds compile-time distinctness only, never runtime checks.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement contracts/phase02/Udvt.sol with a Duration UDVT plus an add() helper via using-for, and a function that would not compile if a raw uint256 were passed, with a test in test/phase02/Udvt.t.sol. Done when: forge test passes and the test round-trips wrap/unwrap and asserts add() sums two Durations.

requirements.purpose: Define a zero-cost distinct type, wrap and unwrap it, and identify its ABI representation and conversion restrictions.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why are custom errors cheaper than revert strings, and what data does a caller get?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Revert data is a 4-byte selector + ABI-encoded args instead of a stored string, cutting deploy and revert gas; the caller gets structured, decodable failure data. Pitfall: the caller must decode the selector/args to read it — plain string tooling won't show the values.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a custom error carrying the shortfall and the revert that uses it.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: error InsufficientBalance(uint256 have, uint256 want); ... if (bal < amt) revert InsufficientBalance(bal, amt);

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you use require vs assert, and what does each return on failure?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Use require for preconditions and revert for unconditional/complex exits; either can return empty data, Error(string), or a custom error. assert is for unreachable invariants and returns Panic(uint) (0x11 overflow, 0x12 divide-by-zero, 0x32 OOB). Pitfall: a triggered assert signals a contract bug, not bad user input.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What must a function be to receive ETH, and in what unit is msg.value?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It must be marked payable, else sending value reverts; msg.value is the attached amount in wei for the current call. Pitfall: msg.value is the same across internal calls in one context — summing it per internal call double-counts the actual ETH received.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Compare transfer, send, and call for sending ETH, and state today's recommendation.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: transfer: 2300-gas stipend, reverts on failure. send: same stipend, returns bool. Both are deprecated in current Solidity docs. call{value:}("") forwards available gas by default and returns (bool, bytes); check success. Pitfall: call hands over control, so use checks-effects-interactions or a guard.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a safe ETH send using call that reverts on failure.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: (bool ok, ) = to.call{value: amount}(""); require(ok, "send failed"); — forward the available gas by default and check success.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Which of receive/fallback runs for a given call, and can a contract with neither accept ETH?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Empty calldata + a receive present → receive; otherwise (data, or no receive) → fallback, which must be payable to accept value. A contract with neither rejects plain transfers, though selfdestruct or protocol balance credits can force ETH. Pitfall: transfer/send provide only their fixed stipend to receive/fallback.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does addr.call return, and what two things does it NOT do for you?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Returns (bool success, bytes returndata). It does NOT revert on failure (you must check success) and does NOT verify the target has code — a call to an EOA/empty address returns success = true. Pitfall: ignoring the returned bool silently swallows the callee's revert.

proposedPrompts.promptText: In a delegatecall, whose storage and msg.sender are used, and what is the critical safety requirement?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The caller's storage is read/written and msg.sender/msg.value are preserved from the original call; the target's code runs but address(this) is the caller. Requirement: proxy and implementation storage layouts must match slot-for-slot. Pitfall: a layout mismatch makes the implementation write to the wrong slots and corrupt state.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a delegatecall that forwards a payload and reverts on failure.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: (bool ok, bytes memory data) = impl.delegatecall(msg.data); require(ok); — runs impl's code against this contract's storage.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does staticcall guarantee, and what happens if the callee tries to write state?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It runs the sub-call read-only; any state change — SSTORE, LOG, CREATE, selfdestruct, or value-call — makes the EVM revert the sub-call. Pitfall: invoking a 'view' function through a plain call instead of staticcall loses the read-only guarantee entirely.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What can try/catch handle, and how do you separate a revert string from an arithmetic panic?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Only external calls and new-contract creation (not internal/private). catch Error(string reason) captures require/revert strings; catch Panic(uint code) captures asserts/arithmetic; catch (bytes) catches custom errors; bare catch is the fallback. Pitfall: it cannot catch failures in internal calls, so wrapping your own function in try does nothing.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do abi.encode and abi.encodePacked differ, and why is encodePacked dangerous for hashing?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: abi.encode uses standard 32-byte-word head/tail encoding and is decodable with the schema; encodePacked omits dynamic lengths and concatenates compactly. Pitfall: adjacent dynamic values are ambiguous — ("a","bc") and ("ab","c") have the same packed preimage. Use abi.encode for security-relevant structured hashes.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the hash of two strings in a way that is NOT vulnerable to the packed collision.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: keccak256(abi.encode(a, b)) — standard ABI encoding gives distinct pairs distinct preimages, unlike the ambiguous packed concatenation (apart from the hash function's negligible collision probability).

proposedPrompts.promptText: How is a function selector computed, and why prefer abi.encodeCall over abi.encodeWithSignature?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Selector = bytes4(keccak256("name(type1,type2)")) using canonical types (uint256, not uint); calldata is selector ++ abi.encode(args). Pitfall: encodeWithSignature takes a string that the compiler can't type-check, so a typo mis-encodes silently — encodeCall(IFoo.f, (args)) is verified at compile time.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What kind of hash is keccak256, and what does the encode-vs-packed choice affect?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The pre-standard Keccak-256 (not NIST SHA3-256): deterministic, one-way, collision-resistant, 32-byte output; used for mapping slots, merkle roots, selectors, commit-reveal. Pitfall: hashing abi.encodePacked of dynamic inputs can collide, and keccak256(encode(x)) ≠ keccak256(encodePacked(x)) — pick one deliberately.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does ecrecover return on failure, and name two ways signature verification is abused.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It returns address(0) on failure — you must reject that or a bad sig 'authorizes' the zero address. Pitfall: (1) signature malleability — (r, n−s) is a second valid signature — enforce low-s; (2) replay — reuse the same signature — bind a nonce/deadline and the verifying contract/chain (EIP-712). Prefer OpenZeppelin's ECDSA.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the recovery of a signer from an EIP-191 personal-signed 32-byte hash.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: bytes32 d = keccak256(abi.encodePacked("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32", hash)); address signer = ecrecover(d, v, r, s); require(signer != address(0));

proposedPrompts.promptText: What goes into an EIP-712 domain separator, and why does it matter for replay?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Common domain fields are name, version, chainId, and verifyingContract; the digest is keccak256("\x19\x01" ++ domainSeparator ++ hashStruct(msg)). These fields separate chains/contracts, but EIP-712 alone does not stop same-domain replay — include a nonce/deadline or make the action idempotent.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the final EIP-712 digest given domainSeparator and structHash.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: bytes32 digest = keccak256(abi.encodePacked("\x19\x01", domainSeparator, structHash));

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do internal and external library functions differ, and what can a library not do?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: internal library functions are compiled into the caller and use the internal calling convention; public/external ones use a separately deployed library through DELEGATECALL. A library declares no state, cannot normally receive ETH, and cannot be destroyed. Pitfall: deployed library code runs in the caller's context and must be linked.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What can an interface contain, and what does IToken(addr).f() assume?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Interfaces contain external function signatures and may declare ABI-visible types, events, and errors, but no implementations, state variables, constructor, or modifiers; functions are implicitly virtual. IToken(addr).f() assumes runtime conformance. Pitfall: the type is a compile-time promise, not proof about the address.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does the high-level Contract(addr).f() do that raw call doesn't?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It ABI-encodes from declared types, performs CALL, checks code when needed (or lets return decoding reject empty data), decodes returns, and bubbles failures. A codeless target therefore reverts through a check or decoding. Pitfall: a wrong interface still encodes and interprets data using the wrong schema.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What safety do you give up in an assembly block, and what memory regions must you respect?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: You lose normal type and checked-arithmetic guarantees and can touch memory/storage/calldata directly. Respect scratch 0x00–0x3f, the free-pointer word at 0x40–0x5f, and the zero slot at 0x60–0x7f. Pitfall: corrupting the pointer or zero slot breaks surrounding Solidity allocations.

proposedPrompts.promptText: In Yul, which opcodes read/write storage and memory, and how is a mapping entry's slot located?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: sload/sstore access storage; mload/mstore/mstore8 access memory; keccak256(ptr,len) hashes memory. For a value-type key, mapping m at slot p uses keccak256(abi.encode(key, p)): 32-byte key then 32-byte slot. Pitfall: reversed order, wrong padding, or a bad slot touches unrelated state.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the Yul that computes the storage slot of mapping entry m[key] where m is at baseSlot.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: mstore(0x00, key); mstore(0x20, baseSlot); let slot := keccak256(0x00, 0x40); — uses scratch space for the keccak input.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What is the lifetime and cost of transient storage, and why is it a good reentrancy lock?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: TSTORE and TLOAD each currently cost 100 gas; contract-private transient values survive owned nested frames and are discarded at transaction end. That makes a lock visible to reentrant calls without persistent-storage/refund costs. Pitfall: reset it before a successful return so later calls in the same transaction remain composable.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a reentrancy guard modifier using the transient keyword (0.8.28+).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: bool transient locked; modifier nonReentrant() { require(!locked); locked = true; _; locked = false; } — the transient bool auto-clears at tx end.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does a user-defined value type give you, and what does it NOT do?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: type Duration is uint256 creates a distinct compile-time type converted via Duration.wrap/unwrap, preventing accidental mixing of same-underlying values (Price vs Quantity) at zero runtime cost. Pitfall: it has no operators or implicit conversions by default (add them via using-for since 0.8.19) and adds no runtime checks — only compile-time distinctness.
